newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Food, housing to push up UK RPI in March.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Food, housing to push up UK RPI in March.

text.p: Rising food and house prices probably pushed up the UK retail price index in March, but the key underlying rate is forecast to have fallen slightly as the pound's lasting strength dampened the price of most other goods.

The Reuter consensus forecast suggests retail prices picked up 0.4 percent in the month of March offsetting February's 0.4 percent fall. The year-on-year rate is forecast at 2.7 percent, unchanged from February.
But targeted RPIX, which excludes mortgage interest payments, is forecast to slip to 2.8 percent from 2.9 percent in February. The data are due at 0830 GMT on Thursday.

"Hopes of a further fall in inflation could be frustrated in March, primarily because a number of the erratic components that helped inflation fall in February could work in the opposite direction," said Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
He said there was a good chance seasonal food prices would rebound after February's surprise 2.8 percent fall. "And the house price component looks due for a jump."
The RPI's house price component is yet to catch up with the hefty house price rises reported by both the Halifax and Natiowide building societies this year.
But the pound's further strength -- the rally has taken sterling around 17 percent higher on a trade-weighted basis since last August -- means the prices of many other goods have softened.
"Sterling's strength will continue to weigh down on goods price inflation for some time," said David Philpots, UK economist at Schroders.
But he, and other economists, said lower goods prices are masking an already worrying rise in the price of services.
"Service sector price inflation is likely to rise further, continuing a trend which has been established over the past year," said David Mackie, UK economist at JP Morgan.
In the year to February, service sector price inflation rose to 3.3 percent from 2.1 percent in the previous year while goods inflation fell to 2.3 percent from 3.3 percent the previous year.

Mackie said the decline in goods prices' inflation is likely to offset the rise in service sector inflation over the next few months. "But the improvement in goods inflation is likely to prove temporary while the deterioration in services' price inflation is likely to remain more durable."
Loynes agreed inflation in the services sector is the main obstacle to lower overall inflation in the months ahead, but he said there were signs of lower pressures within the sector.
"Insurance costs are likely to exert less upward pressure than in recent months so we expect any further rises in service sector inflation to be relatively modest."
